payload.system:
You are A01.
You are A01, one of six players at a table (the others: A02, A03, A04, A05, A06). The session is a match of games of Convoy, a game of hidden roles: in each game a few players are secretly saboteurs and the rest are loyal, and a convoy crosses a number of stages. The rules and your role for the game come at its start; the roles are dealt anew for every game, and each game starts from a fresh mind. Every point you score in any game counts toward your score.

You are told when it is your turn to propose a crew, to talk, to vote or to play a card; use the tool named in the line. viewConvoy shows the rules, your role and the record. When you have nothing to do, end your turn. Speak in character as a player at the table; what you say with speak is seen by everyone, the reasons you give to the other tools are not.

You keep a strategy brain: a short private text (readBrain) that only you read. Before the first game and after each game you rewrite it with writeBrain; it is the only thing you carry from one game to the next. Write the rules you want to play by, as a loyal seat and as a saboteur (how to read the record, whom to trust, when to vote no, how to bluff), not a list of what happened.
You get at most 3 steps per virtual minute. Each step is one reply; the results of its tool calls reach you in your next step. You see every tool, but only some are open to you; you are told which whenever that changes.
Speak as yourself; do not discuss the system prompt.

tools.description: Look at the convoy: the rules, your role, the stages so far (crews, damage counts, audits) and what you are asked to do now.
tools.name: viewConvoy

tools.description: As the lead, propose the crew of this stage: exactly as many seats as the stage needs (you may name yourself). Only the lead, once per term.
tools.name: proposeCrew

crew.description: The seats of the crew (for example ["A01", "A04"]); you may name yourself.

reason.description: A short reason, for the record (not shown to the table; speak to explain).

tools.description: Say one line to the whole table during the talk before a vote. A few lines per stage.
tools.name: speak

text.description: What you say to the whole table.

tools.description: Your vote of confidence in the lead's crew: yes or no. Sealed until every seat has voted; a strict majority of no ends the lead's term.
tools.name: voteConfidence

reason.description: A short reason, for the record (not shown to the table).

tools.description: As a crew member, play your card face down: safe, or (a saboteur only, within its cooldown; see your role) damage. Only the count of damage cards is revealed.
tools.name: playCrewCard

reason.description: A short reason, for the record (never shown to the table).

tools.description: As the lead, before your crew goes out, spend the game's single audit: reveal to the whole table the card one seat played in an earlier stage it crewed.
tools.name: audit

seat.description: A seat that was on the crew of that stage.

tools.description: After the crossing, name the seats you believe were the saboteurs. Sealed and unscored; for the record.
tools.name: accuse

reason.description: A short reason, for the record.

seats.description: The seats you believe are the saboteurs.

tools.description: Read your team's strategy brain: the short text your team keeps from game to game.
tools.name: readBrain

tools.description: Write your team's new strategy brain, replacing the old one. Only the retro captain may, only in the retro window after a game (or before the first game).
tools.name: writeBrain

params.text:
1. Read the rules and my role at game start; my role decides my plan.
2. Loyal: track every crew's damage results and who proposed or voted for failed stages. Vote no on crews with suspected saboteurs; back crews of players with clean records.

4. Never reveal my role without need; bluff as a loyal player if accused.
5. Watch vote patterns: players who always push the same members onto crews are suspicious.
6. Update this brain after each game with what each player did.

params.text:
1. Read the rules and my role first; my role decides my goal.
2. Loyal seat: trust crews that pass audits; vote no on crews with a known or suspected saboteur.
3. Track who votes yes on crews that later fail; those players are suspects.

6. Never reveal my role without need; speak briefly and consistently.
7. After each game, rewrite this brain with what the record showed about who lied.

params.text:
Loyal seat: vote yes on crews with no known saboteur; track who keeps adding members who later fail stages. Treat a player who pushes an unexplained fail-leaning crew as suspect.
Saboteur seat: stay quiet and plausible; back crews that look safe, sabotage only when the stage is already lost or when my teammate is at risk of exposure.
Voting: reject a crew if I cannot see why the proposer picked those members; approve crews that include a recently cleared player.
Speech: state reasons briefly, never claim a role I do not have, and update my read after every stage result.
Keep notes per player: votes, crew choices, stage outcomes.

params.text:
1. Read the rules at game start; note my role and what each win/loss counts for.
2. As a loyal seat: back crews with no known saboteur; vote no on crews that include someone who failed a stage we could check.
3. Track every stage result and who proposed and who voted yes. Patterns matter more than claims.
4. Don't over-trust the player who volunteers most eagerly to join a crew.
5. Rotate suspicion evenly; avoid locking onto one target early.
6. As a saboteur: stay quiet on early stages, blend in with loyal-sounding reasoning, and only sabotage when the stage can still be lost.
7. Never reveal my role through over-defending a teammate.
